property_summary: For any inputs to initialize, after it returns the stored baseToken equals the supplied _baseToken (reference preserves assignment), while the mutant that swaps assignment order can be broken when _nft is a contract whose state-setting during its assignment depends on reading baseToken (i.e. ordering-dependent side effects) — so the rule is: c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize returns for all inputs.

After initialize(...) returns, the stored baseToken equals the supplied _baseToken for every input; the mutant (which assigns nft before baseToken) can be observed to violate this when _nft is a contract whose constructor (or state read) performs a call that makes the observed stored baseToken differ due to ordering-dependent side effects.

For every call to initialize(_baseToken,_nft,...) the contract's public baseToken getter must return the exact _baseToken passed; the mutant that assigns nft before baseToken can cause a different baseToken to be observed when _nft is a contract whose fallback/receive (invoked during assignment via external behavior) mutates storage or interferes, so the property will fail for some fuzzed _nft addresses that are contracts.

For every call to initialize(...), after it returns c.baseToken() must equal the provided _baseToken; the mutant that assigns nft before baseToken can be broken when the passed _nft is a contract whose constructor (or code executed when its address is read) reenters or otherwise causes ordering-dependent side-effects so that baseToken is not set as expected.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's baseToken getter must equal the _baseToken argument after initialize returns; the mutant that assigns nft before baseToken can be broken when the supplied _nft is a contract whose assignment (e.g. via a malicious contract that in its fallback/receive triggers a call to the pool) causes ordering-dependent side effects so baseToken ends up different.

For any _feeRate ≤ 5000 accepted by initialize, the contract's feeRate state variable equals the provided _feeRate after initialize returns; the mutant that caps assignment to 5000 will cause feeRate != _feeRate for some valid inputs (when _feeRate > 5000 would have been rejected but we fuzz and include values ≤5000 and also include boundary >5000 to show mutant differs in behavior).

For every admissible initialize(...) call the reference C either accepts the provided fee rate unchanged (feeRate == _feeRate) when the call succeeds; the mutant silently clamps the stored feeRate to 5000 causing feeRate != _feeRate for some admissible inputs (specifically when _feeRate <= 5000 the reference preserves it, while the mutant may change it when _feeRate>5000 is provided and accepted/rejected behaviour differs).

For any call to initialize that succeeds (i.e. does not revert), the reference contract stores feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant, which clamps the stored feeRate to min(_feeRate,5000), will produce a stored feeRate different from _feeRate for some admissible fuzzed _feeRate values and thus violate this property.

For any call to initialize(...) that returns successfully, the contract's stored feeRate equals the _feeRate argument; the mutant clamps the stored feeRate to 5000 (min), so for some fuzzed _feeRate values the stored feeRate will differ and the property will be violated.

For every call to initialize(...) that succeeds, the reference contract stores feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate argument (no clamping), whereas the mutant clamps the stored feeRate to at most 5000 causing feeRate() != _feeRate for some admissible inputs where the call succeeds and _feeRate <= 65535 (the fuzzer will find a value where the mutant's stored value differs).

For any inputs, calling initialize on a fresh C instance either succeeds and leaves initialized == true (reference) — and during the call no reentrant observation can see initialized set early — whereas the mutant sets initialized = true before validating feeRate which can be observed by a reentrant attacker, causing the reference's invariant (that initialize does not appear 'initialized' to reentrant calls before checks complete) to be violated; we test this by fuzzing feeRate and using a reentrant helper whose fallback calls initialize again and observing that the reference never sees the nested initialize succeed while the mutant can.

Calling initialize on a fresh C should never allow a reentrant nested initialize call to observe initialized == true (i.e. nested initialize must revert because outer call hasn't completed); the mutant sets initialized = true early so a reentrant attacker can call initialize reentrantly and succeed, violating that rule.

For any inputs, a correct C never allows a reentrant call to initialize to observe or succeed while the outer initialize is in progress (i.e., any nested initialize attempt during execution of initialize will fail), whereas the mutant that sets initialized = true early can allow a reentrant nested initialize to succeed for some inputs.

During initialize(...) on a fresh C, no reentrant nested call to initialize can succeed (the outer call prevents a nested initialize from completing); the mutant that sets initialized = true early allows a reentrant nested initialize to succeed for some fuzzed feeRate and attacker, breaking this rule.

For any inputs, calling initialize on a fresh C must never allow a reentrant nested initialize call to succeed (i.e. any nested initialize attempt during the outer initialize execution must revert or fail); the mutant that sets initialized = true early can allow a reentrant nested initialize to succeed for some fuzzed inputs, breaking this rule.
